notes: The rules configuration for a v1.0 fleet race (#73): every replay-affecting rules and race-format value, recorded in each race log by ref (ADR 0004).
Rules in 2025 RRS numbering. Units: seconds, degrees, ticks; sizes in hull lengths of the race's boat class, line lengths or fractions of the beat. Schema: docs/rules-file.md.

builderValues (JSON Pointers above) are the values the spec leaves to the builder: the near-miss sweep geometry, the escape simulation's candidates, start tick, 'initially' window and 'changes course' rate, rule 17's tolerances and 'promptly sails astern' window, and the mark-room-given and 'on a beat' tests.
placeholders await tuning: the start row (#35), edge speed retention (#82) and the beat-sizing calibration factor (#80, #105).

Version 2 is version 1 plus raceFormat.startRow.minimumSpacingHullLengths (schema 2, #85): the closest a squeeze of the start row off land (#82) brings neighbours, centre to centre, so they stay clear ahead and clear astern (#35) with a quarter of a hull between them. A placeholder, like the rest of the start row.

Version 3 is version 2 plus raceFormat.penalty.stackedPenaltyDeadlines (schema 3, #89): sequential (G4). Owed penalty turns are served in order, and each turn's deadlines run from its own call or from when the turn before it is completed, whichever is later. A file before schema 3 means fromCall: each turn's clock runs from its own call. Its penalty deadlines are also looser than #9's 15 s and 30 s (the owner, 2026-09-27): started by 20 s and completed by 40 s.

Version 4 is version 3 plus incidents.escape.changesCourseDegreesPerSecond (schema 4, #92): 12. The escape simulation judges room under rules 15 and 16.1, and the right-of-way boat changes course (16.1) on a tick her heading turns faster than this. The autohelm following shifts and puffs turns a boat sailing clean at most about 5.7 deg/s (gusty-offshore@3, the fastest of the four conditions files, 16 boats for 10 minutes on 4 seeds; #228), and stalled at an edge at the class's 10 deg/s floor; a luff is 30-36 deg/s. A file before schema 4 has none: no escape simulation, and rules 15 and 16.1 are never called.

Version 5 is version 4 plus incidents.properCourse (schema 5, #345): rule 17. A boat that becomes overlapped to leeward from clear astern within distanceHullLengths (2, the RRS's) of the other shall not sail above her proper course while they stay overlapped on the same tack within it. Proper course is defined by fiat (#343): the upwind groove on her tack on a beat, the bearing to the mark on a reach, the bearing to the further gate mark or finish line end on a run, kept to the downwind groove. Above is closer to the wind than proper course less the tolerance: 5 degrees on a beat (the pinch allowance), 8 on a reach or run (leeway included). The exception: a boat that, both boats projected on at their velocities, ends clear astern of the other within promptlyAsternSeconds (4) is promptly sailing astern. A file before schema 5 has none: rule 17 is never called.

Version 6 is version 5 plus raceFormat.penalty.turn (schema 6, #487): tackAndGybe. A penalty turn is one tack and one gybe made turning the same way, in either order (RRS 44.2), counted at the boom's crossings: the heading turned between them costs and earns nothing, and turning back without crossing the wind keeps the crossing made. A crossing on a tick her heading didn't turn (a wind shift flipping the boom), or while she is in the zone of the mark she is rounding or has just rounded, counts for nothing, and completing a rounding stage between the two crossings voids the first. Crossing back (the same kind the other way) undoes the crossing; in her first owed turn it starts the turn the other way, and every later owed turn goes the first one's way. One limit: completed by completeSeconds (40) from the turn's clock, which for a turn that becomes current (called, or the turn before it served) while she is rounding starts when she is clear of the mark (out of the zone), and once started runs on through any later rounding; startSeconds and startedTurnDegrees are gone, so there is no start deadline. Rule 21.2 binds her from the turn's first counting crossing until it is served. A file before schema 6 means fullCircle: 360 degrees one way, as before.
